preamble.summary: Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah navigates the tension between divine judgment and covenant faithfulness. The new covenant prophecy (31:31-34) is rendered with striking literalism. Anti-anthropomorphism governs descriptions of God's emotional response to Israel's unfaithfulness (anger, grief, jealousy). The Messianic 'Branch' passages (23:5, 33:15) receive explicit identification. The Memra functions as the agent of both judgment and future restoration.
preamble.notable_renderings: The call narrative (ch. 1) uses standard anti-anthropomorphic language. The new covenant (31:31-34) is remarkably literal. The Messianic Branch (23:5) is rendered as the righteous Messiah. The Temple sermons use Shekinah language. The confessions of Jeremiah receive minimal theological adjustment, preserving the prophet's raw emotion.
preamble.theological_themes: The Memra as agent of prophetic commissioning and covenant renewal; Shekinah departure and return as the theological framework for exile and restoration; Messianic Branch theology; the new covenant as Torah internalization; anti-anthropomorphism in divine pathos.

renderings.hebrew_text: בְּטֶרֶם אֶצָּרְךָ בַבֶּטֶן יְדַעְתִּיךָ
renderings.targum_text: ad la tzayartakh bemeiayya yeda'atakh
renderings.targum_rendering: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.
renderings.mt_rendering: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.
notes: Jeremiah's calling is rendered literally. Divine foreknowledge is not an anthropomorphism requiring adjustment — it is an attribute of God's eternal knowledge.

renderings.hebrew_text: וַיִּשְׁלַח יְהוָה אֶת־יָדוֹ וַיַּגַּע עַל־פִּי
renderings.targum_text: ushedar Adonai yat pitgam nvu'ateih visamkha al pumi
renderings.targum_rendering: And the LORD sent forth the word of his prophecy and placed it upon my mouth.
renderings.mt_rendering: Then the LORD put out his hand and touched my mouth.
notes: God's hand reaching out and touching Jeremiah's mouth becomes 'the word of his prophecy' being placed upon Jeremiah's mouth. The physical gesture is replaced with verbal prophetic commissioning — the Word, not the hand, empowers the prophet.

renderings.hebrew_text: מָה אַתָּה רֹאֶה יִרְמְיָהוּ וָאֹמַר מַקֵּל שָׁקֵד אֲנִי רֹאֶה
renderings.targum_text: ma at chazei yirmiya va'amrit chuttar deluz ana chazei
renderings.targum_rendering: What do you see, Jeremiah? I said: I see a branch of an almond tree.
renderings.mt_rendering: What do you see, Jeremiah? And I said: I see an almond branch.
notes: The opening prophetic vision. The Hebrew wordplay shaqed ('almond') / shoqed ('watching') is preserved in the Targum's literal rendering — the same wordplay foundation appears in v. 12 (the LORD is 'watching' over his word). The Targum cannot reproduce the wordplay but preserves the literal almond image.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי אִתְּךָ אֲנִי נְאֻם יְהוָה לְהַצִּילֶךָ
renderings.targum_text: arei Memri besiyyakhah amar Adonai leshezavutakh
renderings.targum_rendering: For my Memra is in your help, says the LORD, to deliver you.
renderings.mt_rendering: For I am with you, declares the LORD, to deliver you.
notes: The promise of divine presence to the prophet follows the standard Memra formula. Jeremiah's prophetic ministry is sustained by the Memra's accompaniment.

renderings.hebrew_text: אֹתִי עָזְבוּ מְקוֹר מַיִם חַיִּים לַחְצֹב לָהֶם בֹּארוֹת בֹּארֹת נִשְׁבָּרִים
renderings.targum_text: yat dachalti shavqu mequr mei chayyei limchatzav lehon bei'rin bei'rin teviran
renderings.targum_rendering: They have forsaken the fear of me, the source of living waters, to dig for themselves cisterns — cracked cisterns.
renderings.mt_rendering: They have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed out cisterns for themselves, broken cisterns.
notes: The famous 'fountain of living waters' formulation. Cited at John 4:10-14 (Samaritan woman) and 7:38 ('out of his heart shall flow rivers of living water') as the prophetic basis for Jesus' identification of himself with the source of life.

renderings.hebrew_text: וְאָנֹכִי נְטַעְתִּיךְ שׂוֹרֵק
renderings.targum_text: ve'ana netzei'tikh netza shibḥ'a
renderings.targum_rendering: I planted you a noble vine.
renderings.mt_rendering: Yet I planted you a choice vine.
notes: The Israel-as-vineyard / noble-vine theme. Pairs with Isa 5:1-7. Foundational for John 15's 'I am the true vine.'

renderings.hebrew_text: בָּעֵת הַהִיא יִקְרְאוּ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם כִּסֵּא יְהוָה
renderings.targum_text: be'iddana hahi yitqerun liYerushalem kurseih diyeqara daAdonai
renderings.targum_rendering: At that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the glory of the LORD.
renderings.mt_rendering: At that time Jerusalem shall be called the throne of the LORD.
notes: Jerusalem is not the LORD's throne directly but the throne of his glory (yeqar). The eschatological transformation of Jerusalem is mediated through glory-theology.

renderings.hebrew_text: הִמֹּלוּ לַיהוָה וְהָסִרוּ עָרְלוֹת לְבַבְכֶם
renderings.targum_text: qadishu qodam Adonai ve'attar maktan libbekhon
renderings.targum_rendering: Sanctify yourselves before the LORD, and remove the obstinacy of your hearts.
renderings.mt_rendering: Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and remove the foreskin of your hearts.
notes: The heart-circumcision call. The Targum interprets 'foreskin of heart' as 'obstinacy' (maktan) — the same interpretive sharpening as Acts 7:51 ('stiff-necked, uncircumcised in heart') and Rom 2:29's circumcision-of-the-heart soteriology.

renderings.hebrew_text: כַּבְּסִי מֵרָעָה לִבֵּךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַם
renderings.targum_text: tza'aei meibesa libeikh yerushalem
renderings.targum_rendering: Wash your heart from evil, O Jerusalem.
renderings.mt_rendering: Wash your heart from evil, O Jerusalem.
notes: The wash-the-heart-from-evil call. Foundational for biblical purification theology. Echoed at James 4:8 ('purify your hearts, you double-minded').

renderings.hebrew_text: רָאִיתִי אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְהִנֵּה תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ
renderings.targum_text: chazeit yat ar'a veha hi tziddya verukana
renderings.targum_rendering: I saw the land, and behold, it was empty and void.
renderings.mt_rendering: I looked on the earth, and behold, it was without form and void.
notes: MARQUEE — Jeremiah's de-creation vision uses the Genesis 1:2 vocabulary (tohu va-bohu). The judgment is portrayed as un-creation. Foundational for biblical apocalyptic theology of creation-reversed-then-renewed.

renderings.hebrew_text: שׁוֹטְטוּ בְּחוּצוֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַם
renderings.targum_text: shut bishqei yerushalem
renderings.targum_rendering: Run through the streets of Jerusalem.
renderings.mt_rendering: Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem.
notes: The Diogenes-of-Jerusalem search-for-righteous formula.

renderings.hebrew_text: הִנְנִי נֹתֵן דְּבָרַי בְּפִיךָ לְאֵשׁ וְהָעָם הַזֶּה עֵצִים
renderings.targum_text: ha ana yahev pitgamai befumakh ke'ishshata ve'amma haden ke'aei
renderings.targum_rendering: Behold, I am putting my words in your mouth like fire, and this people are like wood.
renderings.mt_rendering: Behold, I am making my words in your mouth a fire, and this people wood.
notes: The word-as-fire image. Anticipates Heb 12:29 ('our God is a consuming fire') and Acts 2:3 (Pentecost tongues of fire — divine Word made fire-on-the-tongue).

renderings.hebrew_text: וַיְרַפְּאוּ אֶת שֶׁבֶר עַמִּי עַל נְקַלָּה
renderings.targum_text: ve'aseu yat tevar amma' le'allama
renderings.targum_rendering: And they have healed the wound of my people superficially.
renderings.mt_rendering: They have healed the wound of my people lightly.
notes: The false-prophet critique. Cited (in concept) at Rev 18:22-23 in the Babylon-judgment lament. The 'shallow healing' image is foundational for biblical critique of cheap grace.

renderings.hebrew_text: שִׁאֲלוּ לִנְתִבוֹת עוֹלָם
renderings.targum_text: she'alu lishevilei alma
renderings.targum_rendering: Ask for the paths of old.
renderings.mt_rendering: Ask for the ancient paths.
notes: The 'ask for the ancient paths' call. Foundational for Jewish-Christian traditionalism — the appeal to the wisdom of past generations.

renderings.hebrew_text: הֵיכַל יְהוָה הֵיכַל יְהוָה הֵיכַל יְהוָה הֵמָּה
renderings.targum_text: heikhela daAdonai heikhela daAdonai heikhela daAdonai innun
renderings.targum_rendering: The Temple of the LORD, the Temple of the LORD, the Temple of the LORD are these.
renderings.mt_rendering: The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD are these.
notes: The deceptive refrain is rendered literally — Jonathan preserves the irony of false confidence in the Temple's inviolability.

renderings.hebrew_text: הַמְעָרַת פָּרִצִים הָיָה הַבַּיִת הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר נִקְרָא שְׁמִי עָלָיו בְּעֵינֵיכֶם
renderings.targum_text: ha kemei'arta dechiviye havei beita haden de'itqari shemi alohi be'eineikhon
renderings.targum_rendering: Has this house, which is called by my name, become like a den of thieves in your eyes?
renderings.mt_rendering: Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes?
notes: The Temple Sermon's most famous line. Cited verbatim by Jesus at the Temple cleansing (Matt 21:13 / Mark 11:17 / Luke 19:46): 'My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers.' The Targum's preservation confirms the pre-Christian standardization of the formula.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי לְכוּ נָא אֶל מְקוֹמִי אֲשֶׁר בְּשִׁילוֹ אֲשֶׁר שִׁכַּנְתִּי שְׁמִי שָׁם
renderings.targum_text: arei izelu ke'an le'atri diveShiloh di ashrei Shekhineti tamman
renderings.targum_rendering: For go now to my place which was in Shiloh, where I caused my Shekinah to dwell there.
renderings.mt_rendering: Go now to my place that was in Shiloh, where I made my name dwell at first.
notes: God's 'name dwelling' at Shiloh is rendered as 'Shekinah dwelling' at Shiloh. The destruction of Shiloh is a precedent for Shekinah departure — the Shekinah can leave a sanctuary it once inhabited.

renderings.hebrew_text: הַצֳרִי אֵין בְּגִלְעָד אִם רֹפֵא אֵין שָׁם
renderings.targum_text: ha la qatama de'ila'an be'ar'a degil'ad im aharin asaya leit tamman
renderings.targum_rendering: Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there?
renderings.mt_rendering: Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there?
notes: The 'balm in Gilead' lament — proverbial in English Bible reception. The Negro spiritual 'There Is a Balm in Gilead' takes its title from this passage.

renderings.hebrew_text: מִי יִתֵּן רֹאשִׁי מַיִם וְעֵינִי מְקוֹר דִּמְעָה
renderings.targum_text: ulevai dey'hi reishi mayya ve'einai meqor dim'a
renderings.targum_rendering: Oh that my head were waters and my eye a fountain of tears.
renderings.mt_rendering: Oh that my head were waters, and my eyes a fountain of tears.
notes: The weeping-prophet image — Jeremiah's signature self-presentation. Foundational for biblical lament theology.

renderings.hebrew_text: אַל תִּשְׁמַע לַעֲצַתָּם
renderings.targum_text: la tishemei le'atzatam
renderings.targum_rendering: Do not listen to their counsel.
renderings.mt_rendering: Take heed, every one, of his neighbor.
notes: The do-not-trust-friend warning.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי אִם בְּזֹאת יִתְהַלֵּל הַמִּתְהַלֵּל הַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדֹעַ אוֹתִי
renderings.targum_text: elahein beda yishtevach demishtevach lemiskal ulemidda yathi
renderings.targum_rendering: But in this let the one who boasts boast: that he has insight and knows me.
renderings.mt_rendering: But let him who boasts boast in this: that he understands and knows me.
notes: The boast-in-the-LORD formula. Paul cites this verse at 1 Corinthians 1:31 and 2 Corinthians 10:17 ('let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord') as the Christian alternative to boasting in human achievement.

renderings.hebrew_text: וַיהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֱמֶת הוּא אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם
renderings.targum_text: vaAdonai Elohim hu Elah qeshot hu Elah chayyin umalka de'alma
renderings.targum_rendering: But the LORD God — he is the true God, he is the living God and the eternal King.
renderings.mt_rendering: But the LORD is the true God; he is the living God and the everlasting King.
notes: The confession of God's uniqueness amid idol polemic is rendered literally. Attributes like 'true,' 'living,' and 'eternal king' are non-anthropomorphic and require no adjustment.

renderings.hebrew_text: וִהְיִיתֶם לִי לְעָם וְאָנֹכִי אֶהְיֶה לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים
renderings.targum_text: utehevon qodamai le'am va'ana ehei lekhon le'elaha
renderings.targum_rendering: And you shall be a people before me, and I will be your God.
renderings.mt_rendering: And you shall be my people, and I will be your God.
notes: The bilateral covenant formula. Recurs throughout the OT (Lev 26:12, Jer 7:23, 30:22, 31:33, Ezek 36:28). Cited at 2 Cor 6:16, Heb 8:10, Rev 21:3 as the eschatological-covenant promise.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי אֶת רַגְלִים רַצְתָּה וַיַּלְאוּךָ וְאֵיךְ תְּתַחֲרֶה אֶת הַסּוּסִים
renderings.targum_text: arei im im rigaltayya rahatat va'a'tu yatakh ve'eikhdein ttitcharei im susvavayya
renderings.targum_rendering: If you have run with footmen and they have wearied you, how will you compete with horses?
renderings.mt_rendering: If you have raced with men on foot and they have wearied you, how will you compete with horses?
notes: Divine response to Jeremiah's complaint. The 'racing with horses' image — used metaphorically in Christian spiritual writing for the escalating challenges of the spiritual life.

renderings.hebrew_text: הֲיַהֲפֹךְ כּוּשִׁי עוֹרוֹ וְנָמֵר חֲבַרְבֻּרֹתָיו
renderings.targum_text: ha yithappekh kushaya mishakh venimra raqamohi
renderings.targum_rendering: Can the Cushite change his skin or the leopard his spots?
renderings.mt_rendering: Can the Ethiopian change his skin or the leopard his spots?
notes: The classic 'leopard cannot change spots' image. Foundational metaphor for human moral incapacity — echoed in Christian total-depravity theology.

renderings.hebrew_text: אִם עֲוֺנֵינוּ עָנוּ בָנוּ יְהוָה עֲשֵׂה לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ
renderings.targum_text: im chovavanna asivu banna Adonai avid bedil shemakh
renderings.targum_rendering: Though our iniquities testify against us, O LORD, act for the sake of your name.
renderings.mt_rendering: Though our iniquities testify against us, act, O LORD, for your name's sake.
notes: The act-for-your-name's-sake intercession. Foundational for biblical for-the-sake-of-the-name theology.

renderings.hebrew_text: מִקְוֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹשִׁיעוֹ בְּעֵת צָרָה
renderings.targum_text: miqveh yisrael upharkeih be'idana de'aqa
renderings.targum_rendering: Hope of Israel, his deliverer in the time of trouble.
renderings.mt_rendering: Hope of Israel, its savior in time of trouble.
notes: The 'Hope of Israel' messianic title. Cited at Acts 28:20 by Paul ('it is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain').

renderings.hebrew_text: וְאַתָּה בְקִרְבֵּנוּ יְהוָה
renderings.targum_text: ve'att shechintakh shariya beinanna Adonai
renderings.targum_rendering: And your Shekinah dwells in our midst, O LORD.
renderings.mt_rendering: Yet you, O LORD, are in the midst of us.
notes: Shekinah-substitution in Jeremiah's drought-prayer. The Shekinah-in-the-midst formula is central to OT Israel-as-divine-dwelling theology.

renderings.hebrew_text: נִמְצְאוּ דְבָרֶיךָ וָאֹכְלֵם
renderings.targum_text: ishtekachu pitgamakh va'aqabbleinun be'inah
renderings.targum_rendering: Your words were found, and I received them with delight.
renderings.mt_rendering: Your words were found, and I ate them.
notes: Jeremiah's metaphor of consuming the divine word. Echoed at Ezekiel 3:1-3 (eating the scroll), Revelation 10:9-10 (the angel's scroll), and the broader Christian Lectio Divina tradition of internalizing scripture.

renderings.hebrew_text: אֵלֶיךָ גּוֹיִם יָבֹאוּ מֵאַפְסֵי אָרֶץ
renderings.targum_text: qodamakh ammin yei'tun missayfei ar'a
renderings.targum_rendering: To you shall the nations come from the ends of the earth.
renderings.mt_rendering: To you shall the nations come from the ends of the earth.
notes: The eschatological-pilgrimage theme — gentiles drawn to YHWH. Echoes Isa 2:2-3, 60:3 and is fulfilled in Christian missionary expansion (Acts 1:8, Rev 21:24).

renderings.hebrew_text: אָרוּר הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר יִבְטַח בָּאָדָם
renderings.targum_text: lit gevra dirhetz be'enasha
renderings.targum_rendering: Cursed is the man who trusts in a human.
renderings.mt_rendering: Cursed is the man who trusts in man.
notes: The trust-no-flesh warning. Pairs with v. 7's blessed-is-the-man-who-trusts-in-the-LORD.

renderings.hebrew_text: בָּרוּךְ הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר יִבְטַח בַּיהוָה
renderings.targum_text: berikh gevra dirhetz bemeimra deAdonai
renderings.targum_rendering: Blessed is the man who trusts in the Memra of the LORD.
renderings.mt_rendering: Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD.
notes: Pre-Nicene Tier S — the Memra as object of trust. Parallels Psalm 1's 'blessed is the man.' The Targum's faith-in-Memra formula reinforces the pattern of Memra as a hypostatic object of trust (cf. Exod 14:31, Deut 1:32).

renderings.hebrew_text: עָקֹב הַלֵּב מִכֹּל וְאָנֻשׁ הוּא מִי יֵדָעֶנּוּ
renderings.targum_text: saggi sariv liba mikkol vetaqqif lechado man yidda yatei
renderings.targum_rendering: Most exceedingly perverse is the heart, and very strong; who can know it?
renderings.mt_rendering: The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?
notes: The classic anthropological pessimism: human heart-deceit is unknowable from within. The Reformation's reading of total depravity draws explicitly on this verse. The Targum's saggi sariv ('most exceedingly perverse') intensifies the MT's already strong language.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּסֵּא כָבוֹד מָרוֹם מֵרִאשׁוֹן מְקוֹם מִקְדָּשֵׁנוּ
renderings.targum_text: kursei yeqara de'illaya min qadmai atar beit maqdashana
renderings.targum_rendering: The throne of glory on high from the beginning is the place of our Temple.
renderings.mt_rendering: A glorious throne set on high from the beginning is the place of our sanctuary.
notes: The heavenly throne of glory corresponds to the earthly Temple. Jonathan establishes the two-tiered cosmology: the heavenly throne and the earthly sanctuary mirror each other.

renderings.hebrew_text: רְפָאֵנִי יְהוָה וְאֵרָפֵא
renderings.targum_text: asseini Adonai ve'eitassei
renderings.targum_rendering: Heal me, O LORD, and I shall be healed.
renderings.mt_rendering: Heal me, O LORD, and I shall be healed.
notes: Jeremiah's healing-prayer. Echoed at Luke 4:23 ('physician, heal yourself') and the broader OT healing vocabulary.

renderings.hebrew_text: כְּחֹמֶר בְּיַד הַיּוֹצֵר כֵּן אַתֶּם בְּיָדִי בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
renderings.targum_text: kechemar bida defachara ken atton qodami beit yisrael
renderings.targum_rendering: Like clay in the potter's hand, so are you before me, O house of Israel.
renderings.mt_rendering: Like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel.
notes: The potter-and-clay image. The MT's 'in my hand' is rendered qodami ('before me') — the standard Onkelos/Jonathan move to avoid divine-hand anthropomorphism. The image is foundational to Paul's potter-clay argument at Romans 9:21.

renderings.hebrew_text: שׁוּבוּ נָא אִישׁ מִדַּרְכּוֹ הָרָעָה
renderings.targum_text: tuvu kean gevar me'urcheih bishta
renderings.targum_rendering: Return, every one of you, from his evil way.
renderings.mt_rendering: Return, every one from his evil way.
notes: The repentance-imperative. Foundational for the prophetic and Christian repentance theology (Acts 2:38, 3:19).

renderings.hebrew_text: וְהָיָה בְלִבִּי כְּאֵשׁ בֹּעֶרֶת עָצֻר בְּעַצְמֹתָי
renderings.targum_text: vahava belibbi ke'eishata medliqa atzira begarmai
renderings.targum_rendering: And it was in my heart like a burning fire, shut up in my bones.
renderings.mt_rendering: It was in my heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones.
notes: The prophetic compulsion — Jeremiah cannot suppress the divine word. The fire-in-bones image becomes a paradigmatic description of prophetic vocation in Jewish and Christian spiritual writing.

renderings.hebrew_text: עֲשׂוּ מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה
renderings.targum_text: iv'idu dina utzedaqta
renderings.targum_rendering: Do justice and righteousness.
renderings.mt_rendering: Do justice and righteousness.
notes: The royal-justice command. Echoed throughout the prophetic literature (Mic 6:8, Isa 1:17). Foundational for biblical social-ethics.

renderings.hebrew_text: הוֹי בֹּנֶה בֵיתוֹ בְּלֹא צֶדֶק
renderings.targum_text: vai devanei beiteih bela qushta
renderings.targum_rendering: Woe to him who builds his house without justice.
renderings.mt_rendering: Woe to him who builds his house by unrighteousness.
notes: The royal-justice-violation woe. Foundational for biblical theology of accountability of leaders.

renderings.hebrew_text: חַי אָנִי נְאֻם יְהוָה כִּי אִם יִהְיֶה כָּנְיָהוּ
renderings.targum_text: qayyam ana amar Adonai im yehei khanyahu
renderings.targum_rendering: As I live, says the LORD, even if Coniah were [a signet].
renderings.mt_rendering: As I live, declares the LORD, though Coniah were a signet.
notes: The Coniah/Jeconiah curse. Removes the Davidic line from any Coniah-descendant — relevant to NT genealogies (Matt 1:11-16 traces through Jeconiah but via Joseph the legal-but-not-biological father).

renderings.hebrew_text: הוֹי רֹעִים מְאַבְּדִים וּמְפִצִים אֶת צֹאן מַרְעִיתִי
renderings.targum_text: vai parnasi memabdin umvadrin yat ana der'iti
renderings.targum_rendering: Woe to the leaders who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture.
renderings.mt_rendering: Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture.
notes: The wicked-shepherds critique — sets up the messianic shepherd promise of v. 5. Foundational for John 10's Good Shepherd / hireling distinction.

renderings.hebrew_text: הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים נְאֻם יְהוָה וַהֲקִמֹתִי לְדָוִד צֶמַח צַדִּיק
renderings.targum_text: ha yomayya atyin amar Adonai va'aqim leDavid Meshicha zakkaya
renderings.targum_rendering: Behold, the days are coming, says the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Messiah.
renderings.mt_rendering: Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch.
notes: The 'righteous Branch' (tsemach tsaddiq) is rendered 'righteous Messiah' (Meshicha zakkaya). Jonathan explicitly decodes the botanical metaphor as Messianic prophecy, consistent with his treatment of Isaiah 11:1. The Branch is the Messiah.

renderings.hebrew_text: וְזֶה שְּׁמוֹ אֲשֶׁר יִקְרְאוֹ יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ
renderings.targum_text: veden shemeih di yiqreinnei Adonai tzidqana
renderings.targum_rendering: And this is the name by which he shall be called: the LORD is our righteousness.
renderings.mt_rendering: And this is the name by which he will be called: 'The LORD is our righteousness.'
notes: The Messiah's throne name 'YHWH-Tsidqenu' is preserved literally. Jonathan does not shy away from a name that applies YHWH to the Messianic king, though it can be read as a statement about God rather than an identification of the Messiah with God.

renderings.hebrew_text: הַאֱלֹהֵי מִקָּרֹב אָנִי נְאֻם יְהוָה וְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי מֵרָחֹק
renderings.targum_text: ha elaha de'ithgli al ar'a ana amar Adonai ve'ana elaha demhalla'in shaqif maleh
renderings.targum_rendering: Am I a God who reveals himself only on earth, says the LORD, and am I not also a God who watches from afar?
renderings.mt_rendering: Am I a God at hand, declares the LORD, and not a God afar off?
notes: The omnipresence question is paraphrased to avoid the difficulty of locating God. The Targum's reformulation makes God's presence universally revelatory rather than spatially near or far.

renderings.hebrew_text: אִם יִסָּתֵר אִישׁ בַּמִּסְתָּרִים וַאֲנִי לֹא אֶרְאֶנּוּ
renderings.targum_text: im yittammar gevar bemissatraya ve'ana la chazei leih
renderings.targum_rendering: If a man hides in secret places, can I not see him?
renderings.mt_rendering: Can a man hide himself in secret places so that I cannot see him?
notes: Divine omniscience formula. Echoed at Hebrews 4:13 ('no creature is hidden from his sight, but all are naked and exposed to the eyes of him with whom we have to do').

renderings.hebrew_text: הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ נְאֻם יְהוָה וּכְפַטִּישׁ יְפֹצֵץ סָלָע
renderings.targum_text: ha la kheidnan pitgamai ke'ishshata amar Adonai ukhefatish dimefatzetz tinra
renderings.targum_rendering: Is not my word like fire, says the LORD, and like a hammer that breaks rock?
renderings.mt_rendering: Is not my word like fire, declares the LORD, and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces?
notes: The divine word as fire and hammer. Cited at Hebrews 4:12 ('the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword'). The Targum preserves the literal force of the word's penetrating power.

renderings.hebrew_text: וְעָבְדוּ הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה אֶת מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה
renderings.targum_text: veyifelechun ammayya ha'illein yat malka devavel shav'in shenin
renderings.targum_rendering: And these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
renderings.mt_rendering: And these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
notes: The seventy-years-of-exile prophecy. Cited at Daniel 9:2 (Daniel's reading of Jeremiah triggers his Seventy-Weeks vision) — foundational for biblical chronology and apocalyptic timing. Also echoed at 2 Chr 36:21.

renderings.hebrew_text: קַח אֶת כּוֹס הַיַּיִן הַחֵמָה הַזֹּאת
renderings.targum_text: deber yat kasa dechamar lewata haden
renderings.targum_rendering: Take this cup of the wine of wrath.
renderings.mt_rendering: Take from my hand this cup of the wine of wrath.
notes: The cup-of-wrath image. Echoed at Matt 26:39 (Jesus' Gethsemane prayer 'let this cup pass from me') and Rev 14:10, 16:19, 18:6 (the eschatological cup of God's wrath).

renderings.hebrew_text: יְהוָה מִמָּרוֹם יִשְׁאָג
renderings.targum_text: Adonai min merom beit Shekhinteih yigbirah qaleih
renderings.targum_rendering: The LORD from the height of the house of his Shekinah shall raise his voice.
renderings.mt_rendering: The LORD will roar from on high.
notes: 'On high' becomes 'the height of the house of his Shekinah,' localizing the heavenly source of judgment in Shekinah cosmology. God does not 'roar' (an animal metaphor) but 'raises his voice.'

renderings.hebrew_text: אָנֹכִי עָשִׂיתִי אֶת הָאָרֶץ
renderings.targum_text: ana avadit yat ar'a
renderings.targum_rendering: I have made the earth.
renderings.mt_rendering: It is I who by my great power have made the earth.
notes: The divine-creator claim within a foreign-policy oracle. Sovereignty theology.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי אָנֹכִי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת־הַמַּחֲשָׁבֹת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי חֹשֵׁב עֲלֵיכֶם... מַחְשְׁבוֹת שָׁלוֹם
renderings.targum_text: arei ana yeda'na yat chushebanayya de'ana chashiv aleikhon... chushebanei shelam
renderings.targum_rendering: For I know the thoughts which I think concerning you... thoughts of peace.
renderings.mt_rendering: For I know the plans I have for you... plans for welfare.
notes: God's knowledge of his own plans is rendered literally. Divine planning is an attribute of wisdom, not an anthropomorphism. The promise of peace/welfare is directed to the exiles.

renderings.hebrew_text: וְעָבְדוּ אֵת יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵיהֶם וְאֵת דָּוִד מַלְכָּם אֲשֶׁר אָקִים לָהֶם
renderings.targum_text: viyiphlchun qodam Adonai Elahehon viyishttam'un leMeshicha bar David malkhon di aqim lehon
renderings.targum_rendering: And they shall serve before the LORD their God, and they shall obey the Messiah son of David, their king, whom I will raise up for them.
renderings.mt_rendering: And they shall serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.
notes: 'David their king' is interpreted as 'the Messiah son of David, their king.' Jonathan makes the Messianic identification explicit: the future David is not the historical David resurrected but the Messiah who descends from David's line.

renderings.hebrew_text: וְהָיָה אַדִּירוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וּמֹשְׁלוֹ מִקִּרְבּוֹ יֵצֵא
renderings.targum_text: vihavei rabrehon minnehon uMeshikhon mibeinehon yitgeli
renderings.targum_rendering: And their great one shall be from among them, and their Messiah shall be revealed from their midst.
renderings.mt_rendering: Their prince shall be from themselves; their ruler shall come from their midst.
notes: The ruler 'coming from their midst' becomes the Messiah 'revealed from their midst' (yitgeli). The Messiah does not merely appear — he is revealed, using the same theology of divine disclosure applied throughout Jonathan.

renderings.hebrew_text: וְאַהֲבַת עוֹלָם אֲהַבְתִּיךְ עַל כֵּן מְשַׁכְתִּיךְ חָסֶד
renderings.targum_text: ureshamta de'alma rachimittikh al kein neshakhittikh be'eithevuta
renderings.targum_rendering: And with an everlasting love I have loved you; therefore I have drawn you with faithful kindness.
renderings.mt_rendering: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
notes: The everlasting-love formula. Echoed at John 6:44 ('no one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him') — Jesus reads the Father's drawing-with-love through this Jeremianic frame.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי הָיִיתִי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְאָב
renderings.targum_text: arei Memri havat leYisrael le'abba
renderings.targum_rendering: For my Memra has been a father to Israel.
renderings.mt_rendering: For I am a father to Israel.
notes: God's fatherhood of Israel is mediated through the Memra. Even the most intimate relational metaphor is expressed through the Word, maintaining the Memra as the mode of all divine-human relationship.

renderings.hebrew_text: וְהָפַכְתִּי אֶבְלָם לְשָׂשׂוֹן
renderings.targum_text: ve'ehappekh evlehon lechedva
renderings.targum_rendering: I will turn their mourning into joy.
renderings.mt_rendering: I will turn their mourning into joy.
notes: The mourning-into-joy promise. Echoed at John 16:20 ('your sorrow will be turned into joy').

renderings.hebrew_text: קוֹל בְּרָמָה נִשְׁמָע נְהִי בְּכִי תַמְרוּרִים רָחֵל מְבַכָּה עַל בָּנֶיהָ
renderings.targum_text: qala beramata ishtema'a meliphi bechi tamruri rachel mevakkita al benaha
renderings.targum_rendering: A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and bitter cries — Rachel weeping for her sons.
renderings.mt_rendering: A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping — Rachel weeping for her children.
notes: Cited at Matthew 2:18 in the Massacre of the Innocents narrative. The Targum's preservation of the literal weeping-Rachel image confirms its standardized form before Matthew's citation.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי בָרָא יְהוָה חֲדָשָׁה בָּאָרֶץ נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר
renderings.targum_text: arei bera Adonai chadeita be'ar'a nuqveh tehei tetuv le'oraita
renderings.targum_rendering: For the LORD has created a new thing in the land: a woman shall return to the Torah.
renderings.mt_rendering: For the LORD has created a new thing on the earth: a woman encircles a man.
notes: MARQUEE — the famous 'a woman shall encircle a man.' The Targum's reframing 'a woman shall return to the Torah' is rabbinic-exegetical. Christian tradition (esp. Jerome and the Vulgate's femina circumdabit virum) reads this Mariologically — Mary surrounds Christ in incarnation.

renderings.hebrew_text: הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים נְאֻם יְהוָה וְכָרַתִּי אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל... בְּרִית חֲדָשָׁה
renderings.targum_text: ha yomayya atyin amar Adonai ve'agzar im beit Yisrael... keyam chadatt
renderings.targum_rendering: Behold, the days are coming, says the LORD, when I will make with the house of Israel... a new covenant.
renderings.mt_rendering: Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel.
notes: The new covenant prophecy is rendered with striking literalism. Jonathan does not qualify, restrict, or reinterpret 'new covenant' (keyam chadatt). This is the verse cited in Hebrews 8:8-12 as fulfilled in Christ. The targum's literalism here is remarkable given its tendency to interpret elsewhere.

renderings.hebrew_text: נָתַתִּי אֶת תּוֹרָתִי בְּקִרְבָּם וְעַל לִבָּם אֶכְתְּבֶנָּה
renderings.targum_text: eittein yat oraiti begevvehon ve'al libbehon ikhtevinnah
renderings.targum_rendering: I will put my Torah in their inward parts, and upon their heart I will write it.
renderings.mt_rendering: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts.
notes: The Torah internalization is rendered literally. The new covenant does not replace Torah but internalizes it. Jonathan's treatment suggests the new covenant is Torah-centered renewal, not Torah abolition.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי אֶסְלַח לַעֲוֺנָם וּלְחַטָּאתָם לֹא אֶזְכָּר עוֹד
renderings.targum_text: arei ashbiq lechovehon ulechotehon la edkar tub
renderings.targum_rendering: For I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more.
renderings.mt_rendering: For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.
notes: The climax of the new covenant: divine forgiveness and the end of sin-remembrance. Jonathan renders this literally, preserving the unconditional promise of forgiveness that defines the new covenant.

renderings.hebrew_text: עֹשֶׂה חֶסֶד לַאֲלָפִים וּמְשַׁלֵּם עֲוֺן אָבוֹת אֶל חֵיק בְּנֵיהֶם
renderings.targum_text: avid cheisda le'alfin ulemashallam chovei avahan le'av benayya batreihon
renderings.targum_rendering: Doing kindness for thousands and repaying the iniquity of fathers to the bosom of the children after them.
renderings.mt_rendering: Showing steadfast love to thousands but repaying the iniquity of the fathers to the bosom of their children after them.
notes: The 'visiting iniquity' formula. Echoes the Decalogue's Exodus 20:5-6 / Deut 5:9-10. The 'thousands' are interpreted as thousands of generations (cf. Targum Onkelos at Exodus 20:6). Foundational for Jewish-Christian theology of intergenerational consequence balanced against intergenerational mercy.

renderings.hebrew_text: הִנֵּה אֲנִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי כָּל בָּשָׂר הֲמִמֶּנִּי יִפָּלֵא כָּל דָּבָר
renderings.targum_text: ha ana Adonai elaha dekol bisra ha minni yithkasei kol pitgam
renderings.targum_rendering: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh; is anything hidden from me?
renderings.mt_rendering: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too hard for me?
notes: The 'God of all flesh' epithet. Echoed at Numbers 16:22, 27:16. Foundational for biblical universalism.

renderings.hebrew_text: קְרָא אֵלַי וְאֶעֱנֶךָּ
renderings.targum_text: qari qodamai ve'aqabbel tzelutakh
renderings.targum_rendering: Call to me, and I will receive your prayer.
renderings.mt_rendering: Call to me, and I will answer you.
notes: The call-and-receive promise. Foundational for biblical prayer theology (cf. Matt 7:7, Jer 29:12).

renderings.hebrew_text: וְטִהַרְתִּים מִכָּל עֲוֺנָם
renderings.targum_text: ve'addakkeinun mikkol chovehon
renderings.targum_rendering: And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity.
renderings.mt_rendering: I will cleanse them from all the guilt of their sin.
notes: The cleansing-from-iniquity promise. Echoed at 1 John 1:9.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי טוֹב יְהוָה כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ
renderings.targum_text: arei tav Adonai arei le'alam te'eithevuteih
renderings.targum_rendering: For the LORD is good; for his faithful love endures forever.
renderings.mt_rendering: For the LORD is good, for his steadfast love endures forever.
notes: The classic temple-liturgical refrain. Repeated 26 times in Psalm 136 (Hallel HaGadol). Echoes the Davidic temple-music tradition (1 Chr 16:34, 41; 2 Chr 5:13).

renderings.hebrew_text: בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם וּבָעֵת הַהִיא אַצְמִיחַ לְדָוִד צֶמַח צְדָקָה
renderings.targum_text: beyomayya ha'innun uve'iddana hahi atzammach leDavid Meshicha detzidqa
renderings.targum_rendering: In those days and at that time I will cause to sprout for David a Messiah of righteousness.
renderings.mt_rendering: In those days and at that time I will cause a righteous Branch to spring up for David.
notes: The second Branch prophecy in Jeremiah is also rendered as 'Messiah of righteousness' (Meshicha detzidqa). The agricultural metaphor of sprouting is preserved alongside the Messianic identification.

renderings.hebrew_text: וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא לָהּ יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ
renderings.targum_text: veden di yitqerun lah min qodam Adonai bidqayin yitaseyan lana
renderings.targum_rendering: And this is the name by which she [Jerusalem] will be called: 'Before the LORD our righteousness will be accomplished for us.'
renderings.mt_rendering: And this is the name by which it will be called: 'The LORD is our righteousness.'
notes: While 23:6 applied the name to the Messianic king, 33:16 applies it to Jerusalem. Jonathan renders the city's name as a theological statement: before the LORD, righteousness is accomplished. The name YHWH-Tsidqenu has both personal (Messianic) and civic (Jerusalem) applications.

renderings.hebrew_text: וַיִּמְשְׁכוּ אֶת יִרְמְיָהוּ בַּחֲבָלִים וַיַּעֲלוּ אֹתוֹ מִן הַבּוֹר
renderings.targum_text: uneshakhu yat yirmiya behavlin ve'asseiqu yatei min guba
renderings.targum_rendering: And they pulled Jeremiah up with ropes and lifted him from the cistern.
renderings.mt_rendering: Then they drew Jeremiah up with ropes and lifted him out of the cistern.
notes: The Ebed-Melech rescue. Foundational for biblical rescue-from-pit theology (cf. Ps 40:2 'he drew me up from the desolate pit'). Cited typologically in Christian readings of Christ's descent and ascent.

renderings.hebrew_text: כִּי אִתְּךָ אָנִי נְאֻם יְהוָה לְהוֹשִׁעֶךָ
renderings.targum_text: arei Memri besiyyakhah amar Adonai leshezavutakh
renderings.targum_rendering: For my Memra is in your help, says the LORD, to save you.
renderings.mt_rendering: For I am with you, declares the LORD, to save you.
notes: The concluding promise to Jacob/Israel uses the standard Memra-help formula. Even amid oracles against the nations, God's relationship with Israel is Memra-mediated.

renderings.hebrew_text: יָבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵמָּה וּבְנֵי יְהוּדָה יַחְדָּו
renderings.targum_text: yei'tun benei yisrael innun uvenei yehudah kachada
renderings.targum_rendering: The sons of Israel and the sons of Judah shall come together.
renderings.mt_rendering: The people of Israel and the people of Judah shall come together.
notes: The reunification-of-Israel-and-Judah promise. Echoes Ezek 37:15-23 (the joined-stick prophecy). Eschatological theme.

renderings.hebrew_text: צֹאן אֹבְדוֹת הָיָה עַמִּי
renderings.targum_text: ana de'avad havva ammi
renderings.targum_rendering: My people have been like lost sheep.
renderings.mt_rendering: My people have been lost sheep.
notes: The 'lost sheep' divine-shepherd formula. Echoed at Matt 10:6 ('the lost sheep of the house of Israel') and Luke 15 (the parable of the lost sheep).

renderings.hebrew_text: גֹּאֲלָם חָזָק יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת שְׁמוֹ
renderings.targum_text: paroqahon taqqif shemei Adonai tzevaot shemei
renderings.targum_rendering: Their Redeemer is strong; his name is the LORD of hosts.
renderings.mt_rendering: Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name.
notes: The Redeemer-of-Israel formula. Foundational for biblical redemption theology.

renderings.hebrew_text: רִפִּינוּ אֶת בָּבֶל וְלֹא נִרְפָּתָה
renderings.targum_text: asseinanha levavel vela itasiat
renderings.targum_rendering: We tried to heal Babylon, but she was not healed.
renderings.mt_rendering: We would have healed Babylon, but she was not healed.
notes: The Babylon-judgment context — adopted by Revelation 18 for the eschatological Babylon. Cited (in concept) at Rev 18:5 ('her sins are heaped high as heaven').

renderings.hebrew_text: וְשִׁלַּמְתִּי לְבָבֶל וּלְכֹל יוֹשְׁבֵי כַשְׂדִּים
renderings.targum_text: ve'ashalem levavel uleyatevei kasda'ei
renderings.targum_rendering: I will repay Babylon and all who dwell in Chaldea.
renderings.mt_rendering: I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea.
notes: The Babylon-judgment promise. Foundational for Revelation 18's eschatological-Babylon.
